summary: Streaming chat responses stall or disconnect mid-generation (SSE/WebSocket) after recent latency regression
description: Issue summary: Customers reported streaming chat responses either disconnecting or stalling mid-generation over SSE and WebSocket transports following a spike in inference latency observed after the 2026-02-20 runtime/edge deploy. Impact: Several enterprise customers (notably AcmePayments Inc.) saw mid-stream disconnects or producers that emitted only partial text, resulting in degraded UX and support escalations. Environment: prod | us-east-1; streaming via API gateway -> streaming-proxy -> serving-runtime. Affected models: redwood-1.2 and gpt-4o-mini. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start a long-form chat generation (> 600 tokens) using SSE or WebSocket to the /v1/chat/stream endpoint pinned to redwood-1.2 in us-east-1. 2) Observe initial tokens stream within expected latency, then either: a) connection closes with client error "connection closed by server"; or b) stream stalls (no data) for 30-90s and then the connection resets. Observed behavior / logs: - streaming-proxy logs show repeated "upstream reset" and "client disconnected" entries around the same timestamps as customer reports. - nginx/api-gateway logs show intermittent 502/504 with upstream read timeout after ~60s. - serving-runtime traces show tail-token generation taking longer than usual (p50->p95 increased from 40ms->220ms per token for some workloads) starting at 2026-02-20T03:10Z. - TCP level logs show RSTs and FINs from proxies; no TLS errors. Hypotheses investigated: 1) Autoscaler shred/scale-down killing in-flight workers during long streams. 2) Proxy timeout/config change introduced in 2026-02-20 deploy that aggressively closes idle streaming connections. 3) Inference runtime CPU contention causing prolonged per-token latencies that hit proxy timeouts. Temporary workaround: - Advise customer to pin to dedicated capacity (if available) or shorter max tokens while we investigate. - Increase client-side retry/ resume logic if using websocket resumption (where applicable). - Support enabled request-level retry fallback to non-streaming (polling) mode for critical flows.

resolution_summary: Root cause: a 2026-02-20 change to streaming-proxy (PR 482) introduced buffering and reduced idle keepalive timeout from 120s to 60s. For long-tail token generation workloads the proxy closed connections between tokens or buffered single-frame writes, causing clients to see stalls or connection resets. Fix: rolled back the timeout change for streaming routes and disabled the new buffering path for SSE/WebSocket; patched proxy in PR 489 and deployed to us-east-1. Also added a runtime metric (streaming_write_delay_ms), updated alerting for streaming.disconnect_rate, and added a short-term mitigation to autoscaler to avoid scale-downs during active streams. Customer confirmed behaviour returned to normal after deploy.

notes: Post-incident: added an automated canary test that runs a long-stream (1k tokens) against streaming endpoint after edge/proxy changes. Also created a Grafana dashboard for stream_write_delay and disconnect_rate. Customer (AcmePayments) asked for a 30-day postmortem; PM/Eng to coordinate.
